title: Tracing samples for ML-quality regression detection
body:
Purpose:
Provide a pragmatic tracing sampling strategy and associated dashboard guidance that increases the signal-to-noise for detecting ML quality regressions (hallucination rate, response divergence, repeated tokens, embedding drift) without exploding storage/query costs. This is a working sketch: intent is to align SRE, Applied ML, and Product so we can run tighter experiments and faster rollbacks.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated inference paths where we can attach trace/span metadata.
- Focus on post-generation signals (model outputs) correlated with traces collected during request processing.
- Not a full instrumentation spec (that lives in infra repo); this is a sampling+dashboard-level plan.

Background / motivation:
We often see quality regressions (small prompt changes, model variant swaps, quantization regressions) that don’t trigger latency/error alerts but do increase subtle failure signals. Full trace capture for every request is prohibitively expensive; naive uniform sampling misses rare failure cohorts. We need a hybrid sampling policy to efficiently collect traces that are most useful to root-cause ML-quality issues.

Key concepts and signals to surface:
- ML-quality signals (examples): hallucination_flag (binary heuristic), user_reported_fail, repetition_score (>threshold), response_logprob_delta (avg token logprob drop), semantic-embedding-drift (embedding cosine difference from baseline), safety-filter-fires.
- Trace anchors: model_version, route_id, prompt_template_id, tenant_id (if multi-tenant), sequence_length, kv_cache_hit, generation_latency_ms. Anchors tie traces to high-level cohorts.
- Cohort triggers: derived boolean or score used to increase sampling probability (see policy).

Sampling policy (hybrid, tiered):
1) Baseline reservoir: 0.5% uniformly sampled traces across all requests (keeps historical context).
2) Heuristic upsampling (10–50x): if a request has any of the ML-quality signals above soft thresholds, sample with higher probability. Example heuristics: hallucination_flag == true -> 40% sample; repetition_score > 0.6 -> 25% sample; logprob_delta < -1.5 -> 30% sample; safety-filter-fires -> 100% sample (we must capture those).
3) Deterministic cohort capture: always capture first N requests for a new model_version or recent rollout bucket (e.g., first 10k requests after rollout) to establish baseline.
4) Stratified tail capture: for high-latency or high-token-length tails (>= 95th percentile for route), sample at 5–20% to investigate long-context failure modes.
5) Adaptive feedback loop: downstream alerting or evaluation harness marks candidate prompts as suspicious (via webhook); automatically raise sampling to 100% for matching prompt_template_id for a short window (30 minutes) to gather immediate diagnostic data.

Implementation notes (practical):
- Tag traces with minimal but high-value metadata only (avoid including full prompt). Include prompt_hash and prompt_template_id; keep raw prompt out of default traces to protect PII and reduce size. If needed, fetch full prompt from secure store keyed by prompt_hash under restricted access.
- Use streaming trace chunks for multi-stage generation to avoid re-sending entire sequence in trace payload.
- Keep span cardinality low: turn tenant_id into tenant_bucket for dashboards (e.g., top-10 tenants plus "other").
- Persist a compact quality summary per trace (small JSON fields): {h_flags, rep_score, logprob_delta, emb_drift_score} to enable fast queries without full-text scanning.

Dashboard layout suggestions (compact investigative view):
- Top row: global counters for suspicious events (hallucination_rate, safety_fires, avg_emb_drift) with short timeframe toggles (1h/6h/24h).
- Middle row: cohort heatmap (model_version x route_id) showing relative change in hallucination_rate vs baseline. Clicking a cell opens a trace list filtered by sampling reason.
- Right-side: recent rollout view (model_version timeline) showing deterministic capture progress and cumulative quality delta.
- Bottom: trace anchors panel: distribution graphs for sequence_length, generation_latency, kv_cache_hit fraction for the filtered cohort. Include quick links to open raw traces (obfuscated prompts).
- Cost-control widget: estimated storage cost for the selected sampling window and buttons to throttle sampling back to baseline.

Query examples (pseudo-SQL / tracing DSL):
- Find high-emb-drift traces in last 24h:
  SELECT trace_id, model_version, route_id, emb_drift_score, timestamp
  FROM traces
  WHERE emb_drift_score > 0.25 AND timestamp > now() - interval '24h'
  ORDER BY emb_drift_score DESC
- Trace list for hallucination_flag with sampling reason:
  SELECT trace_id, sampling_reason, tenant_bucket, generation_latency_ms
  FROM traces
  WHERE hallucination_flag = true AND sampling_reason IS NOT NULL
  LIMIT 200

Alerting and runbook hooks:
- Alert rule examples:
  - S1: hallucination_rate (24h) increases by +2.5 percentage points and absolute > 1.5% for prod routes -> Pager, run rapid cohort capture (force 100% sampling for matching templates for 1h).
  - S2: embedding-drift population avg > 0.15 for model_version compared to baseline -> Notify ML owners, open regression investigation ticket.
- Runbook quick steps:
  1) Check cohort heatmap for affected routes/model_version.
  2) Pull deterministic traces (first N of rollout) and heuristic-upsampled traces; compare top-k frequent prompt_template_ids.
  3) Reproduce locally against the same model_version and tokenization (use recorded prompt_hash).
  4) If reproduction confirms regression, rollback to previous model_version or toggle quantization profile; instrument canary with deterministic capture.

Privacy and access considerations:
- Default traces must redact any PII. Use prompt_hash and gated fetch flows for full-text retrieval limited to compliance-approved roles.
- Storage retention: upsampled traces for quality regressions should be retained for 90 days; baseline reservoir for 365 days (for longitudinal drift analysis).

Instrumentation checklist for infra/APIs:
- Emit compact quality summary fields at generation end.
- Sampling decision must be made at the request runtime with flags that record sampling_reason(s) on the trace.
- Expose an API for evaluation/harness to request temporary elevated sampling for specific prompt_template_id or tenant_bucket.
- Make sampling config overridable per deployment (hosted/dedicated/private).

Dashboard UX/Investigative notes (operational tips):
- Pre-bake a set of "investigate" filters: by model_version, prompt_template_id, tenant_bucket, sampling_reason. Those should map to pre-signed queries so operators can click-to-run.
- Provide a compact summary line in each trace row (score vector) so operators can triage without opening the full trace.
- Avoid panels that require expensive join queries; keep most panels driven by the compact summary indices.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default soft thresholds for heuristic scores (run sensitivity sweep in staging).
- Storage/retention budget: what is acceptable monthly ingestion for upsampled traces? (need finance input).
- Integration with Customer Success flow for user-reported failures (webhook -> sampling).

Appendix: Example sampling config snippet (pseudocode):
- baseline_rate: 0.005
- heuristics: [
    {name: "hallucination_flag", prob: 0.4},
    {name: "rep_score_gt_0_6", prob: 0.25},
    {name: "logprob_delta_lt_-1_5", prob: 0.3},
    {name: "safety_fire", prob: 1.0}
  ]
- deterministic_capture: {on_new_model_version: 10000}

Notes to self: gather feedback from Applied ML next sync (Ethan), validate cost impact with infra telemetry (Sofia), and draft a minimal PR to add sampling_reason to trace schema (Devika).
